entries.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a revised Slate palette design image using the user's new reference.
REFERENCE ROLES: image1 is the user's LIGHT color picker, the dominant design reference for restrained proportions and structure; image2 is the user's dimension-stringer reference, the dominant dimension style; image3 when supplied is an OLD option to revise, preserving its broad layout identity only. Replace its tall bulky form controls and black value badges.

This revision is FLAT, RESTRAINED, LOW PROFILE. Use an unobtrusive wide shallow color field, three very thin rails (checkerboard transparency, neutral value/brightness, rainbow hue), a single unobtrusive bottom row of eyedropper, recent color dots, and RGB values. Tiny round slider thumbs; minimal padding; NO large headings inside the palette, NO chunky input boxes, NO pill-shaped RGB borders, NO double frames, NO drop shadows, NO glow, NO oversized Apply/Cancel controls, NO detached modal. Color-picker gradients are functional; all geometry and other surfaces are FLAT solid color. Tools have quiet thin outline glyphs in compact SQUIRCLE containers, never circular button containers.

IMPORTANT NUMERIC INTERACTION: Every numeric value is text that can be edited DIRECTLY AT ITS CURRENT LOCATION. All RGB channels, opacity, brightness, hue, radius, stroke width, and dimensions follow this. Resting values have no visible input box. Focused value has only a thin underline, subtle selection highlight and text caret. No pencil-button launchers or separate value editor windows. RGB example 'R 18%' 'G 83%' 'B 75%' for teal; one RGB row only. Each color rail may have a very small directly editable endpoint value such as '100%', '83%', '173°', avoiding bulky labels. Do not repeat RGB or show technical labels such as U8.

RECENT COLORS: show six modest solid-color dots once each, newest first: teal, muted coral, ochre, lavender, slate-blue, charcoal. They are a deduplicated DOCUMENT RECENT-COLOR HISTORY, not a fixed rainbow palette. No duplicates or endless dots. An unboxed desktop eyedropper glyph sits to their left. A tiny caption outside the mockup may say 'Recent document colors · newest first'. In-app swatches don't need a caption.

DARK THEME unless specified otherwise: canvas #0e1013, very subtle palette backing #14161a, border #333941, white-gray text #dde2e8, muted #878e96, accent teal #2dd4bf, selection and dimensions pale blue #6fb7ff. Palette border nearly disappears. Icons from Slate's quiet outline family: paint bucket for Fill, outline circle for Stroke, corner outline for Corners; their CONTAINERS are squircles like the primary toolbar. The active button has restrained teal stroke/fill, not neon. No ornamental stylization.

SPATIAL LAYOUT: selected teal rectangle below a compact three-squircle strip; open editor immediately ABOVE the active button, growing upward away from rectangle. The editor's height should be noticeably LESS than the selected rectangle's height, about 55–70% of rectangle height for Fill, much less for Corners. All components form one anchored assembly that will scale in world/board space, including typography and gaps. No screen-edge inspector. Never overlap the shape. Keep the complete assembly compact within the image.

DIMENSIONS match user's image2: thin blue external extension lines, a parallel baseline BELOW the rectangle and another RIGHT of it, small diagonal architectural end ticks. Blue text '180 u' centered IN A GAP in the bottom line; '120 u' rotated 90 degrees and centered IN A GAP in the right line. Text aligned WITH its stringer, including the vertical one. NO black badge backgrounds, NO value boxes, NO text sitting below or off the dimension baseline. The canvas itself shows through the line gap. Editing happens right in the line gap.

Composition: clean landscape design sheet, restrained small title in the margin. Normally two examples side by side: Fill editor open on left, Corners editor open on right. Both rectangles sit on the same baseline at same scale. The right rectangle is lightly filleted; active Fillet and Percent state with directly editable '50%'. Corners uses two compact text/icon binary choices Fillet/Chamfer and Units/% plus ONE fine slider and its inline value. Avoid enormous segmented tiles. All text crisp and small relative to shape, with orderly space. These are realistic desktop UI mockups, not marketing graphics.

Title 'A · Low-profile stack'. Revise the prior Focused stack: ONE shallow palette above the selected Fill squircle, width approximately the shape width. Color field is a WIDE SHORT rectangle, about 4:1 aspect ratio, followed by the three thin horizontal rails and then a single compact bottom row of desktop-eyedropper glyph, six recent dots, and RGB text values. Keep the entire picker about half the height of the selected rectangle, no header. Numeric fields are plain directly-editable text; show the G83% value with a fine underline to hint interactivity. Right Corners editor is exceptionally shallow: compact Fillet/Chamfer text choices on one line; Units/% and a slender radius rail with editable50% on the second. Percent and Fillet selected. No panel pointer triangles. Preserve squircle toolbar and user's exact external dimension aesthetic.
entries.correction: Precision revision of image1, use image2 only as the exact dimension reference. Preserve the dark theme, both shapes, all three squircle buttons above each shape, six unique recent color dots, RGB direct editing, and shallow color field with three rails. Fix dimensions on BOTH shapes: MOVE the blue180u text UP to be ON its bottom dimension line, and interrupt that line with a gap around the text. MOVE each vertical120u label ONTO its right dimension line, keeping it rotated90 degrees, and interrupt the line around it. Exactly like image2. No badges or boxes. Make the right Corners editor much lower profile: remove the large filled segment tiles; use quiet short text choices Fillet / Chamfer on one row, Units / % beside them, and a thin radius rail with unboxed underlined50% on a second row. Fillet and% remain visibly selected with restrained teal text/underline only. The corners palette bottom should remain close above its toolbar, while its top moves down as it becomes shorter. Keep fill editor geometry and every color control exactly unchanged. Flat surfaces, no glow or added windows.
